title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Handbook
author: Sophie Martinez
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Operations guide for Redwood Inference hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities required to run those processes consistently. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, hiring panel organizers, and People Ops partners.

Quick links
- Hiring process checklist (section A)
- New hire onboarding & 30/60/90 plan (section B)
- Performance & feedback cycle (section C)
- Manager playbook (section D)

A. Hiring: process, roles, and standard practices

1) Goal and scope
- Objective: Hire high-quality, diverse candidates who align with Redwood’s values and role-specific competencies while minimizing time-to-offer and recruiter/manager time spent.
- Scope: All full-time employees, contractors with engagements > 6 months, and engineering interns.

2) Roles & responsibilities
- Hiring manager: defines role, approves job description, designs interview loop, and owns final hiring decision with People Ops support.
- Recruiter (People Ops): sources candidates, coordinates interviews, manages offers, and runs background/reference checks.
- Interviewers: evaluate candidates using standardized scorecards and provide timely, evidence-based feedback.
- Hiring committee (IC5+ and management hires): calibrates senior-level hiring and approves offers above band midpoint.

3) Standard hiring workflow
1. Requisition created: hiring manager submits requisition form (HR portal template) and obtains approvals from Director and Finance for net-new headcount.
2. Posting & sourcing: recruiter posts to careers page, LinkedIn, internal referrals, university pipelines, and partner boards. Diversity-sourcing bucket used for all public requisitions.
3. Recruiter screen: 30-45 minute phone screen for interest, basic qualifications, compensation expectations, and logistics.
4. Interview loop: 3-5 interviews depending on level. Required: at least one behavioral/leadership interview and one cross-functional partner. Use role-specific loop template.
5. Debrief & packet: hiring manager consolidates scorecards within 48 hours; recruiter prepares compensation benchmarking and offer recommendation.
6. Offer & background checks: People Ops issues offer letter using the standard template; candidate signs and background/reference checks are initiated.
7. Pre-boarding kickoff: People Ops schedules pre-boarding touchpoints, confirms start date, and coordinates IT/hardware provisioning.

4) Interview loops & scorecards
- Use canonical interview loop templates (Engineering, Product, Sales) from the Interview Loop library.
- Scorecard fields: Role expectations (must-have), Technical competency, Problem solving, Collaboration/communication, Culture fit & values, Overall recommendation.
- Scoring guidance: 1-5 numeric scale. A hire is recommended when majority of interviewers score 4+. Hiring manager documents rationale when proceeding with mixed scores.

5) Offer guidance & compensation
- Base comp bands are maintained in the compensation matrix (/confluence/company-handbook/compensation-bands-2026).
- Any offer above band midpoint requires approval from the VP of the function or People Ops Director.
- Equity and sign-on guidance follow standard templates; recruiter verifies country-specific legal/benefit constraints before finalizing offers.

6) SLAs & time-to-fill targets
- Target time-to-offer (requisition open to offer): 35 calendar days.
- Recruiter-to-manager SLA: initial candidate shortlist within 14 days of posting.
- Interviewer feedback: submitted within 48 hours of interview.

B. New hire onboarding: pre-boarding, Day 1, and 30/60/90 plan

1) Pre-boarding (2-14 days before start)
- People Ops actions: send welcome email and onboarding packet, collect HR documents, schedule start call, create IT ticket for accounts and hardware, add to payroll/benefits.
- Manager actions: send welcome note with first-week agenda, confirm start time and location, assign a buddy and set expectations for first month.
- New hire receives access to the onboarding Confluence space and required training links.

2) Day 1 sample agenda
- Morning: Office/remote setup, HR welcome & benefits overview, ID/KYC tasks.
- Midday: Manager 1:1 (role expectations, immediate priorities), team lunch (virtual or onsite).
- Afternoon: IT access verification, security & compliance training (mandatory), initial project overview and first task assignment.

3) Week 1 deliverables
- Complete mandatory trainings (security, data handling, Code of Conduct).
- Meet with direct manager, assigned buddy, and primary cross-functional partners.
- Complete one low-risk onboarding task (codebase walkthrough, documentation update, or non-production bugfix).

4) 30/60/90 day plan (manager-owned)
- 30 days: Understand systems and team processes; deliver a small scoped task; demonstrate baseline competency.
- 60 days: Lead a component of a project; show increased autonomy and collaboration; submit self-assessment to manager.
- 90 days: Assume primary ownership of core responsibilities; present a 90-day summary to manager and People Ops.

5) Manager onboarding responsibilities
- Weekly 1:1s for the first 90 days (at least twice per week in the first month is recommended).
- Define and document clear success criteria for 30/60/90 milestones in the onboarding plan.
- Conduct a midpoint check at ~45 days and a formal 90-day review submitted to People Ops.

C. Performance & feedback cycle

1) Cadence & objectives
- Annual performance cycle with quarterly checkpoints. Official ratings and comp decisions occur in the annual review window (Q1 for most teams).
- Managers run quarterly check-ins to set goals, review mid-quarter progress, and reflect at quarter end.
- Goal types: company/team OKRs plus SMART goals at the individual level.

2) Formal reviews & calibration
- Managers draft reviews and gather cross-functional feedback. Reviews are submitted to People Ops two weeks prior to calibration.
- Calibration meetings ensure fairness and consistency; outcomes inform promotions and band movements.

3) Continuous feedback & coaching
- Regular 1:1 cadence (weekly/bi-weekly) with documented development conversations in the private manager notes system.
- Use structured feedback (Praise / Improve / Action) and surface concerns early.
- For significant performance issues: engage People Ops early. A formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is used only after documented coaching and reasonable improvement time.

4) Promotion & career pathing
- Promotion criteria align to the competency frameworks and expected impact per level. Managers prepare promotion packets with recent work, 360 feedback, and ladder justification. People Ops coordinates final approvals and compensation adjustments.

D. Manager playbook: hiring, onboarding, coaching, and difficult conversations

1) Hiring manager best practices
- Write outcomes-based job descriptions and identify 3 success metrics for the first 6-12 months.
- Ensure diverse candidate slates and use structured scorecards in interviews.
- Complete annual interview training covering unconscious bias and structured interviewing techniques.

2) Onboarding & early development
- Provide a documented 30/60/90 plan and store it in the onboarding Confluence page.
- Assign a buddy and schedule shadowing sessions during the first month.

3) Ongoing development & coaching
- Hold career conversations every 6-8 weeks and refresh development plans quarterly.
- Encourage use of the learning stipend and align training to competencies and growth goals.

4) Managing performance issues & exits
- Document concerns promptly and escalate to People Ops before initiating a formal performance process.
- Exit process: follow the Exit Checklist to offboard in payroll, revoke IT access, conduct an exit interview, and collect company property.

E. Policies & standard templates (high level)

1) Time off & hybrid work
- PTO: flexible policy requiring manager approval and adherence to minimum guidelines in the Time Off policy.
- Hybrid work: typical expectation: 2-3 onsite days per week for product and engineering teams; exceptions require manager + People Ops approval.

2) Parental leave & caregiver support
- Parental leave follows local regulations plus Redwood top-up policy. Managers coordinate timing and return-to-work plans with People Ops.

3) Code of Conduct & security training
- Mandatory annual completion for all employees. Report violations to HR and Security immediately.

F. Templates & checklists (examples)

1) Sample interview scorecard (short)
- Candidate: ___________________
- Role: _______________________
- Interviewer: _________________
- Date: _______________________
- Scores: Technical (1-5), Problem Solving (1-5), Communication (1-5), Culture Fit (1-5)
- Recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / No hire

2) Onboarding checklist (abbreviated)
| Item | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---:|---:|
| Offer accepted & paperwork completed | People Ops | Pre-start |
| Hardware ordered | IT | Pre-start (two weeks) |
| Accounts provisioned (Slack, Jira, GitHub) | IT | Day 0-1 |
| Security training completed | New hire | Day 1-7 |
| 30/60/90 plan documented | Manager | Day 7 |

3) Exit checklist (abbreviated)
- Notify People Ops & IT (manager)
- Revoke system access (IT)
- Final payroll & benefits reconciliation (Finance / People Ops)
- Exit interview scheduled (People Ops)

G. Governance, reporting, and metrics
- Hiring funnel metrics: applicants, screen-to-interview conversion, offer acceptance rate, time-to-offer. Target offer acceptance >= 70%.
- Onboarding metrics: ramp to full contribution (manager self-report), 90-day mandatory training completion rate (target 95%).
- Performance metrics: promotion velocity, calibration variance, and proportion of managers completing review training (target 100% annually).

H. Related resources & references
- Interview Loop templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/interview-loop-templates
- Compensation bands & promotion policy: /confluence/company-handbook/compensation-bands-2026
- HRIS & benefits portal: https://hr.redwood-inference.internal (internal only)
- People Ops contact: people-ops@redwood-inference.com

Document maintenance
- Owners: People Ops (primary), Hiring Managers (secondary).
- Review cadence: annually or when policy/regulatory changes occur.
